   282	The generate C source subcommand
   283	^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   284	
   285	Generate `C` source code from given database.
   286	
   287	The generated code contains:
   288	
   289	- Message `structs`_.
   290	
   291	- Message `pack`_ and `unpack`_ functions.
   292	
   293	- Signal `encode`_ and `decode`_ functions.
   294	
   295	- Frame id, length, type, cycle time and signal choices `defines`_.
   296	
   297	Known limitations:
   298	
   299	- The maximum signal size is 64 bits, which in practice is never
   300	  exceeded.
   301	
   302	Below is an example of how to generate C source code from a
   303	database. The database is ``tests/files/dbc/motohawk.dbc``.
   304	
   305	.. code-block:: text
   306	
   307	   $ python3 -m cantools generate_c_source tests/files/dbc/motohawk.dbc
   308	   Successfully generated motohawk.h and motohawk.c.
   309	
   310	See `motohawk.h`_ and `motohawk.c`_ for the contents of the generated
   311	files.
   312	
   313	In this example we use ``--use-float`` so floating point numbers in the generated
   314	code are single precision (``float``) instead of double precision (``double``).
   315	
   316	.. code-block:: text
   317	
   318	   $ python3 -m cantools generate_c_source --use-float tests/files/dbc/motohawk.dbc
   319	   Successfully generated motohawk.h and motohawk.c.
   320	
   321	In the next example we use ``--database-name`` to set a custom
   322	namespace for all generated types, defines and functions. The output
   323	file names are also changed by this option.
   324	
   325	.. code-block:: text
   326	
   327	   $ python3 -m cantools generate_c_source --database-name my_database_name tests/files/dbc/motohawk.dbc
   328	   Successfully generated my_database_name.h and my_database_name.c.
   329	
   330	See `my_database_name.h`_ and `my_database_name.c`_ for the contents
   331	of the generated files.
   332	
   333	In the next example we use ``--no-floating-point-numbers`` to generate
   334	code without floating point types, i.e. ``float`` and ``double``.
   335	
   336	.. code-block:: text
   337	
   338	   $ python3 -m cantools generate_c_source --no-floating-point-numbers tests/files/dbc/motohawk.dbc
   339	   Successfully generated motohawk.h and motohawk.c.
   340	
   341	See `motohawk_no_floating_point_numbers.h`_ and
   342	`motohawk_no_floating_point_numbers.c`_ for the contents of the
   343	generated files.
   344	
   345	In the last example ``--node`` is used to generate
   346	message pack functions only for messages sent by the specified node and unpack
   347	functions only for messages with its signal receivers belonging to that node. 
   348	
   349	.. code-block:: text
   350	
   351	   $ cantools generate_c_source tests/files/dbc/motohawk.dbc --node PCM1
   352	   Successfully generated motohawk.h and motohawk.c.
   353	
   354	See `motohawk_sender_node.h`_ and
   355	`motohawk_sender_node.c`_ for the contents of the
   356	generated files.

     4	from typing import Union

     6	from ..database import Message

     9	class SnakeOilAuthenticator:
    10	    """A snake oil authenticator for secure on-board communication
    11	
    12	    The sole purpose of this class is to demonstrate how SecOC can be
    13	    implemented using cantools. These algorithms are in no way
    14	    cryptographically secure! DO NOT USE THEM IN THE REAL WORLD!
    15	    """
    16	    def __init__(self,
    17	                 secret: Union[bytes, str]) -> None:
    18	        if isinstance(secret, bytes):
    19	            self._secret = secret.decode('utf-8')
    20	        else:
    21	            self._secret = str(secret)
    22	
    23	    def __call__(self,
    24	                 dbmsg: Message,
    25	                 auth_data: bytearray,
    26	                 freshness_value: int) \
    27	                -> bytearray:
    28	
    29	        v0 = freshness_value%253
    30	
    31	        # XOR the secret and the data which we ought to authenticate
    32	        result = bytearray([v0]*5)
    33	        for i in range(len(auth_data)):
    34	            result[i % len(result)] ^= auth_data[i]
    35	            result[i % len(result)] ^= self._secret[i%len(self._secret)]
    36	
    37	        return result

     1	# Utilities for dealing with AUTOSAR secure on-board communication.
     2	# (SecOC, i.e., verification of the authenticity of the sender of
     3	# messages.)
     4	
     5	import bitstruct
     6	
     7	from ..database.can.message import Message
     8	from ..errors import Error
     9	from ..typechecking import (
    10	    SecOCAuthenticatorFn,
    11	)
    12	
    13	
    14	class SecOCError(Error):
    15	    """Exception that is raised if something SecOC related goes wrong.
    16	
    17	    """
    18	
    19	
    20	def compute_authenticator(raw_payload: bytes,
    21	                          dbmsg: Message,
    22	                          authenticator_fn: SecOCAuthenticatorFn,
    23	                          freshness_value: int) \
    24	                          -> bytes:
    25	    """Given a byte-like object that contains the encoded signals to be
    26	    send, compute the full authenticator SecOC value.
    27	    """
    28	
    29	    if dbmsg.autosar is None or dbmsg.autosar.secoc is None:
    30	        raise SecOCError(f'Message "{dbmsg.name}" is not secured')
    31	
    32	    secoc_props = dbmsg.autosar.secoc
    33	    n_fresh = secoc_props.freshness_bit_length
    34	    payload_len = secoc_props.payload_length
    35	
    36	    # build the data that needs to be passed to authentificator function
    37	    auth_data = bitstruct.pack(f'u16' # data ID
    38	                               f'r{payload_len*8}' # payload to be secured
    39	                               f'u{n_fresh}', # freshness value
    40	                               secoc_props.data_id,
    41	                               raw_payload[:payload_len],
    42	                               freshness_value)
    43	
    44	    # compute authenticator value
    45	    return authenticator_fn(dbmsg, auth_data, freshness_value)
    46	
    47	def apply_authenticator(raw_payload: bytes,
    48	                        dbmsg: Message,
    49	                        authenticator_fn: SecOCAuthenticatorFn,
    50	                        freshness_value: int) \
    51	                        -> bytearray:
    52	    """Given a byte-like object that contains the encoded signals to be
    53	    send, compute the full message which ought to be send.
    54	
    55	    This is basically the concatenation of the raw payload, the
    56	    truncated freshness value and the truncated authenticator for the
    57	    message.
    58	    """
    59	
    60	    if dbmsg.autosar is None:
    61	        raise RuntimeError(f'Message "{dbmsg.name}" does not have '
    62	                           f'AUTOSAR specific properties.')
    63	    elif dbmsg.autosar.secoc is None:
    64	        raise RuntimeError(f'Message "{dbmsg.name}" does not have any'
    65	                           f'SecOC properties (message is not secured).')
    66	
    67	    result = bytearray(raw_payload)
    68	
    69	    # compute authenticator value
    70	    auth_value = compute_authenticator(raw_payload,
    71	                                       dbmsg,
    72	                                       authenticator_fn,
    73	                                       freshness_value)
    74	
    75	    # get the last N bits of the freshness value.
    76	    secoc_props = dbmsg.autosar.secoc
    77	    n_fresh_tx = secoc_props.freshness_tx_bit_length
    78	    mask = (1 << n_fresh_tx) - 1
    79	    truncated_freshness_value = freshness_value&mask
    80	    payload_len = secoc_props.payload_length
    81	
    82	    bitstruct.pack_into(f'u{n_fresh_tx}r{secoc_props.auth_tx_bit_length}',
    83	                        result,
    84	                        payload_len*8,
    85	                        truncated_freshness_value,
    86	                        auth_value)
    87	
    88	    return result
    89	
    90	def verify_authenticator(raw_payload: bytes,
    91	                         dbmsg: Message,
    92	                         authenticator_fn: SecOCAuthenticatorFn,
    93	                         freshness_value: int) \
    94	                    -> bool:
